newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares continue surge, close some 2 pct up.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares continue surge, close some 2 pct up.

text.p: Italian shares continued their relentless climb on Wednesday, ending just off new Mibtel and Mib30 Bourse index highs set earlier in the day. Traded volumes were not at a record but seen solid at over 2.5 trillion lire, and foreign investors were seen in the front line.

The all-share Mibtel index ended 1.96 percent up at 14,381 after setting a new record high in the afternoon at 14,394. The Mib30 blue chip index closed 1.98 percent up at 21,866 after an earlier peak at 21,925
The Fib30 September futures contract on the Mib30 index ended up 2.72 percent at a new record high of 22,220.
"I saw important counterparties come in and start buying at the slightest blip in stock prices," one dealer said.

Insurances shone with Generali the star of the session, putting on 5.77 percent to 35,786 lire to a new year's high after senior managers told financial analysts the group expected higher premiums and return on equity this year.

Energy giant ENI gained 1.09 percent to 10,228 lire and Fiat put on 3.23 percent to 6,689 while telecoms were all higher with Stet holding 4.26 percent higher at 11,008 lire ahead of its merger with its phone operator unit Telecom Italia which becomes operational on Friday. Telecom rose 2.01 percent to 6,093.

Dealers said that if the stock market rally continued at its current strength it would not be long before the authoritative BCI (Comit) index touched all-time highs, not seen since May 20, 1986 when it was at 908.20.
The Comit index, updated once a day after the end of the session, was at 896.68 on Wednesday, up 14.41 percent.
